why: The AUTHORED half of a feature-ledger row. l6-parity-rows.cjs derives every MEASURED field from a cat6 run artifact and refuses to invent any of these; a spec row id with no entry here refuses BY NAME rather than being written with a guessed route. One block per app, keyed by the row ids in probes/l6-parity.js.
howToAddAnApp: Read the app.s SPECS block in probes/l6-parity.js for its row ids, then write one entry per id. The two destination strings and noLiquidReason are per-app, not per-row.

provenance.dictionary: Copied MECHANICALLY out of the seven dictionary rows already in parity-ledger.json (written by hand on 2026-08-17), in the spec.s own id order, by a one-off node read of the ledger -- not retyped. CORRECTED 2026-09-02: this note used to claim the seventh row, "Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close", had NO spec id and was "deliberately absent". That was false -- `l6-parity.js` declares `{ id: 'windowLifecycle', f: lifecycle }` for every app, and the live run refused BY NAME on it, which is the refusal working. Its four authored fields are now copied from that same ledger row. This block is a REGRESSION TEST -- a live cat6 dictionary run must re-derive these SEVEN features and add ZERO new rows, because the ledger already holds them under the same app-plus-feature keys. Measured 2026-09-02 at 1ec440ab: 7 rows, statuses {both: 7}, added 0.
provenance.calendar: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, and it is the first app whose block was NOT back-derived from an existing ledger row -- parity-ledger.json had no calendar row at all, so all five are new and `added` is expected to be 5, not 0. Every `currentRoute` names the selector the spec.s own `f()` reads, so the authored half cannot drift from the measured half without the run failing. `dataStateOwner` read from src/renderer/calendar.ts (LS_KEYS.calendarEvents in localStorage, mirrored to IDB_KEYS.calendarEvents) and CalendarContent.tsx (mode / cursor / modal are component state, not persisted). Liquid destination read from calendarLiquid.css and the two LiquidSurface call sites at CalendarContent.tsx:391 and :403.
provenance.settings: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, second app with no prior ledger row -- all seven are new. Every currentRoute names the selector the spec.s own f() reads. dataStateOwner separates persisted from not: advancedDisclosure is the only settings row here that survives a reopen (renderer/settingsAdvanced.ts, localStorage jp-settings-advanced-v1), while page, query and scroll are component state. Liquid destination read from the ContextualSurface call sites in SettingsNav.tsx (45, 46, 65, 69) and SettingsApp.tsx:604, and from the pane at SettingsApp.tsx:596-600 which is NOT wrapped.

dictionary.liquidDestination: Same in-window DictionaryView, on the liquid material — `.fwin-liquid` + `data-presentation="liquid"`, body kept on an opaque anchor (L3.2, `20462e3a`)

lookup.feature: Look up a word against the active dictionary source
lookup.keyboardRoute: input is focusable and accepts real keystrokes; a synthetic Enter keydown did NOT trigger a search, so the keyboard route is UNPROVEN, not absent
lookup.dataStateOwner: local JMdict via the main-process dictionary DB

sourceSwitch.feature: Switch dictionary source by language (JA / ZH)

resultActions.feature: Per-result actions: play audio, copy to clipboard history, save to Flashcards, mark New, add to Anki
resultActions.currentRoute: Dictionary window > per-result controls (`Play 食べる`, `Copy to clipboard history`, `Save to Flashcards`, `食べる: New. Click to mark…`, `+ Add to Anki`)

savedSearches.currentRoute: Dictionary window > `Save search` (appears in the Saved searches header)

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close

calendar.standardDestination: CalendarContent in-window: the mode row and date transport above, the month grid / week columns / day list / agenda body below
calendar.liquidDestination: Same in-window CalendarContent on the liquid material — `.fwin-liquid` + `data-presentation="liquid"`. SELECTIVE, not universal: the mode switch and date transport are a `ContextualSurface` (CalendarContent.tsx:391) with the arrows on a bare `AnchorSurface` (:403), while the month grid, week columns, day list and agenda stay plain opaque bodies — a grid of dates is a table, and L2 keeps tables on stable anchors

viewModes.feature: Switch view mode: Month / Week / Day / Agenda
viewModes.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.cal-mode-btn` x4 in the `.cal-context-toolbar` mode row
viewModes.dataStateOwner: component state (`mode`) in CalendarContent.tsx — not persisted, so a reopen returns to Month

monthGrid.feature: Month grid: seven day-of-week headers over a full 42-cell numbered month
monthGrid.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.cal-month-grid` > `.cal-month-dow` x7 + `.cal-month-cell` x42, each carrying a `.cal-month-daynum`
monthGrid.keyboardRoute: cells are click targets; no keyboard grid navigation is claimed here
monthGrid.dataStateOwner: derived from the cursor date; occurrences come from `expandOccurrences` over renderer/calendar.ts events

dateTransport.feature: Move through time: previous / today / next, plus a direct date jump
dateTransport.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.cal-nav` > three buttons + `input[type="date"]`, with the period named in `.cal-header-label`
dateTransport.keyboardRoute: three real buttons and a native date input
dateTransport.dataStateOwner: component state (the cursor date) in CalendarContent.tsx

eventComposer.feature: Create an event: the new-event composer and its cancel recovery
eventComposer.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.calendar-context-head > .btn` opens `.cal-modal`; `.cal-modal-actions` carries save and cancel
eventComposer.keyboardRoute: trigger is a real `type="button"`; the modal is a form of native inputs, selects and a textarea
eventComposer.dataStateOwner: renderer/calendar.ts — `addEvent` writes `LS_KEYS.calendarEvents` in localStorage and mirrors to `IDB_KEYS.calendarEvents`; the open composer itself is component state (`modal`)

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close

settings.standardDestination: SettingsApp in-window: the category rail on the left, the page pane (`role="main"`) on the right
settings.liquidDestination: Same in-window SettingsApp on the liquid material — `.fwin-liquid` + `data-presentation="liquid"`. SELECTIVE: the whole category rail is `ContextualSurface` (SettingsNav.tsx:45, :46, :65, :69) and so is the page header (SettingsApp.tsx:604), while `.os-set-pane-v2` itself stays a plain opaque body — a settings page is a form, and L2 keeps forms on stable anchors

categoryRail.feature: Category rail: the only route to 18 of the 19 settings pages
categoryRail.currentRoute: Settings window > `.os-set-nav-item`, each carrying both a visible label and a `title` (the label is clipped below 420px of `.os-set-body`, so `title` is the narrow tier's only text)
categoryRail.keyboardRoute: real buttons; the current one publishes `aria-current="page"`
categoryRail.dataStateOwner: the item set is derived from settingsRegistry.ts; which one is current is component state (`page`, SettingsApp.tsx:131) and is not persisted

groupedNavigation.feature: Grouped navigation: labelled groups, each list wired to its own label
groupedNavigation.keyboardRoute: each list is a labelled region a screen reader can enumerate; the items inside are buttons
groupedNavigation.dataStateOwner: group membership is declared per entry in settingsRegistry.ts

settingsSearch.feature: Settings search — the second route in, and the one the command palette uses
settingsSearch.currentRoute: Settings window > `.os-set-search-input`, `aria-controls` naming its result panel and `aria-expanded` a real boolean
settingsSearch.keyboardRoute: text input; Escape closes the panel synchronously
settingsSearch.dataStateOwner: `searchSettings()` over settingsRegistry.ts (SettingsSearch.tsx:12); the query itself is component state and is cleared on close

advancedDisclosure.feature: Advanced mode: show or hide the advanced pages, with the rail agreeing with the claim
advancedDisclosure.currentRoute: Settings window > `.os-set-advanced-btn` (`aria-pressed`), advanced rail entries marked by `.os-set-adv-dot`
advancedDisclosure.keyboardRoute: a real toggle button carrying `aria-pressed` and a `title`
advancedDisclosure.dataStateOwner: renderer/settingsAdvanced.ts — persisted in localStorage under `jp-settings-advanced-v1`; UI unlock only, background systems run either way

pageRegion.feature: The page pane names itself after the destination the rail says is current
pageRegion.keyboardRoute: a `main` landmark, reachable by landmark navigation
pageRegion.dataStateOwner: component state (`page`) in SettingsApp.tsx; the label is derived from the same value the rail renders, which is what makes a stale name detectable

homeOverview.feature: Home overview: status chips with real values, and quick cards that are working destinations
homeOverview.currentRoute: Settings window > Home > `.os-set-status-chip` (value in `strong`, caption in `.muted`) + `.os-set-quick-card` (SettingsHome.tsx:69ff, :162)
homeOverview.dataStateOwner: chips read live app state; the cards navigate through the same `page` state the rail uses

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close
